name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,174

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Send brave concluding note

blocks.note: to post a letter is to send it
to brave a danger is to face it

explanation.surface: Someone dispatches a courageous final message at the end of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A postface is the counterpart of a preface: a short piece of writing placed at the end of a book.

clue.text: Drive to contain way of financing public works makes member of family carp

indicators.note: to contain something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to drive forward is to push
the Private Finance Initiative, the British scheme for funding public projects with private money

explanation.surface: A campaign to fund roads and hospitals somehow ends in a fish complaining about the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like a verb meaning to grumble, but it is the fish family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupfish are small desert fishes belonging to the killifish group often called toothcarps, so the clue treats them as carp kin.

clue.text: Middle Eastern music maker variable when turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning letters up means reading them from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a letter used for an unknown quantity in algebra
as in 'as I arrived', meaning when

explanation.surface: A musical instrument from the Middle East behaves unpredictably when it is tuned up.
explanation.definitionFit: The saz is a long-necked lute played across Turkey, Iran and neighbouring lands, so a musical instrument.

clue.text: Fine university dwelling tailored for playwright strongly suited to high life?

definitions.text: for playwright strongly suited to high life

indicators.note: tailored cloth is cut and reshaped, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
standard abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smart college residence has been custom-built to suit a dramatist who loves luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For playwright' marks the word as Shakespeare's: he wrote of a full-winged eagle in Cymbeline.
explanation.definitionFit: Having complete, strong wings makes a bird well equipped for flying high, which the question mark turns into the high life.

clue.text: One taking off supports around skip

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits underneath it

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for around
someone who apes, or takes off, another person is an aper

explanation.surface: A mimic props up a performer who is jumping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests an aircraft; here it means doing an impression of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap or frolic playfully, the same lively movement as to skip about.

clue.text: In Marseilles, I regret taking question in search for contraband

indicators.note: a word taking another takes it in, holding it inside

blocks.note: the French word for I, as spoken in Marseilles
to rue something is to regret it
standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A French speaker apologises for being asked something during a customs inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: The question letter sits inside the regret word, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerque is an old customs term for searching a ship and its papers for smuggled or undeclared goods.

clue.text: Forgotten giant of film at heart of screenplay

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are kept

blocks.note: E.T., Spielberg's film about the extra-terrestrial
the two central letters of this ten-letter word

explanation.surface: A giant from a movie has been lost from the middle of the script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgotten' marks the word as obsolete rather than signalling a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Eten is an archaic word for a giant or ogre, related to ettin, so it is a forgotten term for one.

clue.text: Writ that challenged short citation: nothing about conflict managed

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter goes
one thing placed about another surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: a quote is a citation from a text
zero, shaped like the letter
war is armed conflict
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A legal writ objected to a brief quotation in a carefully handled dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened citation plus the zero form one outer shell, split around the conflict and the managing.
explanation.definitionFit: Quo warranto was a writ demanding by what authority someone held an office or privilege, so challenging that claim.

clue.text: German theologian including King in electronic diagram?

indicators.note: a word including another holds it within its own letters

blocks.note: E is the familiar prefix for electronic, as in e-mail
a chart is a diagram
K is the chess notation for king

explanation.surface: A German scholar of religion turns up as a figure in a circuit diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: The King letter goes inside the diagram word, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Meister Eckhart was a medieval German Dominican mystic and theologian, so he fits the description.

clue.text: Left four nations associated instruction to turn over and fulfil

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for left
four in Roman numerals
the European Union, an association of nations
please turn over, printed at the foot of a page

explanation.surface: A departing group of four countries leaves a note to flip the page and complete the task.
explanation.definitionFit: To live up to an expectation or promise is to meet it in full, which is what fulfilling means.

clue.text: Change tattered Brazil Zoo Upkeep’s A to Z: rewarding if baffling work?

indicators.note: change here asks for one letter in the phrase to be swapped for another
tattered things are torn apart, so these letters come out in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the alphabet is replaced by the last

explanation.surface: A shabby guide to the running costs of a Brazilian zoo gets a revised index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A to Z' looks like a guidebook, but it is an instruction: turn the one A in the phrase into a Z before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of prize puzzles rewards solvers with prizes while setting them baffling problems, as this crossword does.

clue.text: In noyade, drown or immerse revolutionary — powerfully put by poet

indicators.note: in means the letters lie within the words that follow
a revolution turns things round, so the concealed letters run backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A rebel describes mass drownings in the French Revolution in forceful terms.
explanation.walkthrough: A noyade was a mass execution by drowning during the Terror, which makes 'revolutionary' look like part of the scene. Tennyson used the compound in his poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron-worded describes speech that is hard and forceful, a poetic coinage for something stated with power.

clue.text: Found work falsifying vote: true job!

indicators.note: falsifying something distorts it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rigging an election claims it is a genuine bit of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found work' reads like having got a job, but it means a work of art that was found.
explanation.definitionFit: An objet trouvé is an everyday object picked up and displayed as art, so literally a work that was found.

clue.text: First duty, perhaps, for groups in biology

blocks.note: a duty is one kind of tax
A is the first letter, as in grade A

explanation.surface: The top priority in a list of tasks for students of life sciences.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a label: the first tax in a list would be Tax A.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxa is the plural of taxon, any ranked category such as genus or species used in biological classification.

clue.text: Like river with road crossing? Reason not to use it heard

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the words sound, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: a cause is a reason
without a raised road over the water, you would have to wade across

explanation.surface: Someone describes a river with a road over it and wonders why nobody uses the route.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' is the crossing in the definition: if you will not use it, you wade.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a raised road across water or marsh, so a river spanned by one could be called causewayed.

clue.text: Larks greeting sudden changes in direction

blocks.note: an informal hello
a jink is a quick dodging swerve

explanation.surface: Songbirds call out to each other while darting this way and that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Larks' looks like birds, but it means pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Larks in the sense of mischievous fun or pranks are high-spirited antics, the same as boisterous horseplay.

clue.text: Morose Frenchwoman stops exuding warmth and light

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, sitting inside

blocks.note: surly means sullen and bad-tempered
abbreviation of Madame, the French title for a married woman

explanation.surface: A gloomy Frenchwoman suddenly stops being sunny and cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits gloom against warmth; the definition is the last four words, describing a season.
explanation.definitionFit: Summerly means typical of the hot season, which is marked by long bright days and heat.

clue.text: Leaves gatherer maybe wastes energy filling hole in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose it, so a letter is thrown away
filling a gap means sitting inside it

blocks.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
someone clearing fallen leaves with a rake
standard symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A gardener sweeping leaves tires himself out filling a hole, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom for 'so to speak', but it is literally the definition: a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Prakrit names the vernacular Indian languages that grew out of Sanskrit, so it is a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Viewer’s humour after TV laced with ire, I hesitate to say

indicators.note: things laced together are interwoven, mixing up the letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A television watcher's mood after an angry programme, admitted with some reluctance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humour' suggests comedy or temper, but it is the old word for a body fluid; the viewer is the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The vitreum, or vitreous humour, is the clear jelly filling the eyeball, so it belongs to anyone who views.

clue.text: Dismissal uttered by heartless one in environs of veldt?

definitions.text: Dismissal uttered by heartless one in environs of veldt?

indicators.note: without its heart a word keeps only its outside letters
the environs of a place are its outskirts, so only the outside letters stay
in places one piece inside the other
uttered means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound
by means beside, so one part sits next to the other

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
the word with its middle letter removed
getting the sack is being dismissed

explanation.surface: An unkind person out on the South African grassland tells someone to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a rude South African 'get lost', the kind of thing said out on the veldt, which is open grassland there.
explanation.definitionFit: Voetsak is a South African interjection, from Afrikaans, used to tell a dog or person to go away rudely.

clue.text: Old film covering issue of bloody constituent!

indicators.note: a cover goes round what it covers, enclosing it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for old
pic is slang for a film
a person's issue are their children

explanation.surface: A vintage movie depicts the son of a violent character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' reads as an expletive, which the exclamation mark encourages; it literally means of the blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Opsonic relates to opsonins, antibodies in blood serum that prepare bacteria for destruction, so to a part of the blood.

clue.text: Print worker brought over celebrity’s account

indicators.note: something brought over is flipped, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a celebrity is a big name, and the possessive adds the S
standard abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A printer has been called in to give a famous person's version of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A caseman was a compositor, the printing worker who set type by hand from the type case.

clue.text: Wildcat strike may cover area, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to what comes at the very end, here of each word

blocks.note: the final letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: An unofficial walkout might spread across a whole region in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildcat strike' is a set phrase for an unofficial walkout, so the definition hides inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyra is a reddish form of the jaguarundi, a small wild cat of Central and South America.

clue.text: Harry Potter’s targets must include scoundrels

indicators.note: including something means holding it within

blocks.note: in snooker, a potter aims to sink the coloured balls, one of which is the yellow
to harry someone is to dog them, pursuing persistently

explanation.surface: The boy wizard's enemies are said to be villains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry Potter' looks like the wizard, but the two words split: a verb to harass, and a snooker player.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow dog is American slang for a contemptible, cowardly person, so a scoundrel.

clue.text: Flaky stuff in older part as evenly selected

indicators.note: evenly selected means taking the letters in the even-numbered positions

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Peeling material is found in the more ancient section of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepra is a botanical term for the scaly, mealy coating found on some plant surfaces, a flaky substance.

clue.text: Crosses which are awarded for outstanding performance

definitions.text: which are awarded for outstanding performance

blocks.note: first meaning: hybrids, here of yak and domestic cow

blocks.clueFragment: which are awarded for outstanding performance
blocks.note: second meaning: British military decorations for distinguished service

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' looks like medals, which the second half seems to describe, but it means hybrid animals, also spelt dzos or zhos.
explanation.definitionFit: A dso is a Himalayan yak-cow hybrid, and the Distinguished Service Order is a British award for officers' service in combat.

clue.text: Ship’s mystique’s built around large engine component

indicators.note: something built is put together from parts, so the letters are assembled anew
around means the result goes round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, both possessive S letters included
standard abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: The glamour of a vessel has been constructed around something big in its engine room.
explanation.definitionFit: A squish lip system is a combustion-chamber design in diesel engines that drives the air swirl, a part of the engine.

clue.text: Still cycling is common locally

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, the last one coming to the front

blocks.note: still, as in 'not done yet'

explanation.surface: A cyclist who remains on the bike is a familiar sight round here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tye is a dialect word from eastern England for a stretch of shared pasture, the same as a village common.

clue.text: Aircraftman grabbing spy’s withdrawn dagger

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it tight inside
withdrawn means drawn back, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: erk is RAF slang for a lowest-rank aircraftman
to spy something is to see it

explanation.surface: A junior airman seizes a secret agent who has retreated, along with his knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy' reads as a noun, but here it is the verb; the apostrophe S stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kreese is a variant spelling of kris, the Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Demanding return of new official for match plant

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a hard task is a demanding one
standard abbreviation for new
the referee who officiates at a game

explanation.surface: An exacting official insists on returning for the next game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a game but also helps define the official.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard fern is a common evergreen fern of acid woodland and moors, so it is a kind of plant.
